title: A Wolf for the Choir
premise: Casper Villalobos has spent her life as the crown's food-taster, dosing herself with poison to build immunity in a valley where magic cannot follow — and where her own suppressed gift cannot find her. When the usurper Queen announces a hunt for the gifted, Casper is dragged from her valley as bait, for she is the last living vessel of a soul the court beneath the mountain bought and sold decades ago: her mother's. Guided by a disgraced wolf-knight named Sera Aldane and a smuggler who remembers too much, Casper must cross a war-torn country to steal that soul back before the usurper's armies reach the free cities — learning along the way that belonging is not given by blood or law but chosen. In the climax, Casper offers her own hardened body as the vessel to reunite her mother's soul, shattering the court's claim and turning the valley's magic-dead silence into a weapon against the throne; the book ends with the hunt reversed, the free cities holding, and Casper choosing exile-with-family over any crown's pardon.
about_author: Zephyrine Ishikawa is a former line cook turned novelist who writes about people who taste danger for a living. She lives between two mountain ranges and insists both are haunted.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the poison kitchens of the valley keep, Casper sips a laced broth and survives what would kill a duke, cataloguing flavors like prayers. Establishes her routine, her numbness, and the valley's magic-dead quiet. Emotional beat: competent loneliness — she is safe, and it tastes like ash.

chapters.title: A Summons Sealed in Red
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A royal courier arrives with a writ bearing the usurper Queen's seal: all tasters of proven immunity are conscripted for the Great Hunt against the gifted. Casper's keeper tries to burn the writ and dies for it. Emotional beat: dread — the valley's protection ends at its border, and she is being marched past it.

chapters.title: What the Valley Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Casper, first steps beyond the wardline. Magic floods back into her senses — colors sing, stones remember names — and something inside her chest answers, terrifyingly. She meets Sera Aldane, a wolf-knight in chains, also bound for the Hunt. Emotional beat: vertigo and unwanted recognition.

chapters.title: The Queen's Menagerie
chapters.summary: POV Sera. In the royal camp, captured gifted are displayed like animals while officers plan the purge of the free cities. Sera, sentenced for refusing a purge order, studies Casper and realizes what she is: a living reliquary. Emotional beat: cold fury hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Bait Is Still Meat
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The Queen's sorcerer tests Casper's blood and finds the dormant soul-scar — proof she carries stolen goods from the court beneath the mountain. Casper learns her whole life was storage. Emotional beat: betrayal — even her survival was someone else's plan.

chapters.title: Teeth in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Sera. During a night raid by free-city partisans, Sera breaks her own chains, kills her handlers, and offers Casper a choice: stay as the Queen's instrument or run. Casper runs. Emotional beat: the first decision that is entirely hers.

chapters.title: The Smuggler Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Hiding in a river-town, they meet Odile Ferrant, a smuggler whose memory-magic holds the true history of the soul-trade — including the sale of a woman named Luz Villalobos, Casper's mother, to the court beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: grief arriving late, with receipts.

chapters.title: Roads Full of Hunters
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The trio travels toward the free cities ahead of the usurper's armies; checkpoints, burned villages, a near-capture at a toll bridge. Sera teaches Casper to shield her gift. Emotional beat: found-family friction — trust built one argument at a time.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Sing
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Arrival in Vellamare, a city of bells and open magic, where no one flinches at her. For two days Casper experiences belonging without condition — then the war council asks her to be a weapon. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: Terms of War
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The free cities' council debates: flee, fight, or strike the court beneath the mountain to break the Queen's source of bound souls. Only a soul-vessel can enter the vaults alive. Casper volunteers before Sera can object. Emotional beat: love expressed as furious objection.

chapters.title: Lessons in Being a Door
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Training montage of sorts: Odile teaches Casper to open and close the soul-scar; a dying elder gifted shows her how vessels die when they hold too long. Casper confronts what reunion with her mother's soul might actually mean. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The First Fall of Vellamare
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The usurper's vanguard breaches the outer walls; bells crack, streets flood with fire. Sera holds a gate alone and is gravely wounded buying the city an hour. Emotional beat: sacrifice without guarantee — the war is real now.

chapters.title: Underground, Under Contract
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Descending through old trade tunnels toward the court beneath the mountain, Casper reads the ledgers of the soul-trade in the dark — thousands of names, hers among them, filed under assets. Emotional beat: righteous anger finding its target.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The subterranean court receives her as property returning home, courteous and monstrous. Its Steward offers her comfort, permanence, her mother's voice on tap — everything except freedom. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile's past surfaces: she once ran souls for the court before defecting, and the Steward knows it, offering her old debts as leverage. Odile chooses the trio anyway and burns her own name from the ledger. Emotional beat: redemption as an act, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Vault of Voices
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the vault, Casper finds her mother's soul — not a whisper but a whole person, furious and grieving and proud. To carry her out, Casper must open the scar fully, risking dissolution. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness in the same breath.

chapters.title: Everything Owed
chapters.summary: POV Sera, wounded and topside, holding the tunnel mouth against the Queen's hunters as alarms shake the mountain. Sera refuses to retreat, betting everything that Casper will make it out. Emotional beat: faith as a battlefield decision.

chapters.title: Two Heartbeats, One Body
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Climax begins: Casper takes her mother's soul in, and the court's bindings snap taut around them both. Mother and daughter navigate the vault's collapsing wards together, sharing memory, arguing, forgiving. Emotional beat: reunion under mortal pressure.

chapters.title: The Silence Weapon
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Climax: Casper drags the court's power up the mountain and into the magic-dead valley's old wardline, collapsing the court's claim and severing the Queen's soul-source. The Steward unmakes; the mountain exhales. Emotional beat: justice outside every law — done by hand, not decree.

chapters.title: What the Hunt Becomes
chapters.summary: POV Sera. With the soul-source broken, the usurper's armies falter; the free cities counterattack, and the Hunt turns inward on the throne. Sera survives her wounds to see it, and declines a general's commission. Emotional beat: victory that refuses to become ambition.

chapters.title: Luz, Awake
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Aftermath: her mother's soul settles into a restored body grown from the valley's quiet soil — the one place magic couldn't touch her, now the one place she can heal. Casper grieves the years and begins the awkward work of knowing her. Emotional beat: joy with scars.

chapters.title: A Wolf for the Choir
chapters.summary: POV Casper (closing). The crown offers pardons; Casper, Sera, Odile, and Luz decline and settle in the valley, opening its borders to the hunted. The final image: a choir of the once-stolen singing in a kitchen where nothing is poisoned. Emotional beat: belonging, finally chosen and kept.
